content.heading: Interest
content.text: Where and in so far as a decree is for the payment of money, the Court may, in the decree, order interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable to be paid on the principal sum adjudged, from the date of the suit to the date of the decree, in addition to any interest adjudged on such principal sum for any period prior to the institution of the suit, with further interest from the date of the decree to the date of payment or such earlier date as the Court thinks fit. Commercial transactions have a separate enacted rate rule. Read the official text.
